Viṣṇu 85.13: On Mount Nīla.
Viṣṇu 85.14: [He is present] at Kanakhala.
Viṣṇu 85.15: At Kubjāmra.
Viṣṇu 85.16: At Bhṛgutuṅga.
Viṣṇu 85.17: At Kedāra.
In the Mahālaya [section], Viṣṇu 85.18.
Viṣṇu 85.19: At Naḍantikā.
Viṣṇu 85.20: [The fruit] is on the Sugandhā river.
Viṣṇu 85.21: [The Lord is present] at Śākambharī.
Viṣṇu 85.22: At Phalgutīrtha.
Viṣṇu 85.23: [This occurs] at the Mahāgaṅgā.
In the village of Trihalikā, [Viṣṇu 85.24].
Viṣṇu 85.25: At Kumāradhārā.
Viṣṇu 85.26: At Prabhāsa.
"Wherever [one may be] along the Sarasvatī, especially so. (Viṣṇu 85.27)
Viṣṇu 85.28: At Gaṅgādvāra.
And at Prayāga, [one obtains the same merit], O Viṣṇu. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 85.29)
Viṣṇu 85.30: At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean.
Viṣṇu 85.31: [He dwelt] constantly in the Naimiṣa forest.
Especially in Vārāṇasī, [it is taught] in Viṣṇu 85.32.
Viṣṇu 85.33: At the hermitage of Agastya.
Viṣṇu 85.34: At the hermitage of Kaṇva.
In Kauśikī, [as stated in] Viṣṇu 85.35.
On the bank of the Sarayū, [as stated in] Viṣṇu 85.36.
At the confluence of the Śoṇa and the Jyotiṣā, Viṣṇu [is to be worshipped]. (Viṣṇu 85.37)
Viṣṇu 85.38: At Śrīparvata.
Viṣṇu 85.39: At Kālodaka.
At Uttaramānasa, [as stated in] Viṣṇu 85.40.
Viṣṇu 85.41: [The same applies] to the *baḍabā* (submarine fire).
Viṣṇu 85.42: At Mataṅgavāpī.
In the case of the seven sages, [the rule applies] to the seventh generation. (Viṣṇu 85.43)
In the footstep of Viṣṇu (Viṣṇupada).
Viṣṇu 85.45: [He dwells] at the station of the path to heaven.
Viṣṇu 85.46: At the Godāvarī.
Viṣṇu 85.47: At the Gomatī.
Viṣṇu, at the Vetravatī river (85.48).
At the Vipāśā [river], Viṣṇu 85.49.
Viṣṇu 85.50: [The same applies] on the Vitastā.
On the bank of the Śatadrū river. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 85.51)
Viṣṇu 85.52 [mentions] the Candrabhāgā river.
In the Irāvatī [river], Viṣṇu 85.53.
On the bank of the Sindhu river.
Viṣṇu 85.55: At Pañcanada in the south.
Viṣṇu 85.56 enjoins:
In these and other such sacred fords (tīrthas), as well as others.
In the best of rivers, [O] Viṣṇu, 85.58.
Viṣṇu 85.59: Even in all their own natures.
On the sandy banks, Viṣṇu 85.60.
Viṣṇu 85.61: [One should offer] at the springs.
Viṣṇu 85.62: On mountains.
Viṣṇu 85.63: In the groves.
In the forests, [he is] Viṣṇu. 85.64.
In the groves, Viṣṇu 85.65.
In houses smeared with cow-dung, Viṣṇu 85.66.
Viṣṇu 85.67: [One should offer oblations] in beautiful places.
And on this subject, there are these verses sung by the ancestors:
"May that person be born in our family who shall offer us handfuls of water,
especially in rivers abounding in cool water."
"May there arise in our lineage some preeminent man who,
with a concentrated mind, shall perform for us the śrāddha ceremony at the banyan tree of Gayāśīrṣa."
Viṣṇu 85.71a: One should desire many sons, so that even one of them might go to Gayā;
Viṣṇu 85.71c: Or he might perform the Aśvamedha sacrifice, or set free a dark-colored bull.
Viṣṇu 86.01 Now follows the ritual of the release of a bull (vṛṣotsarga).
Viṣṇu 86.02: [One should perform this] on the full moon day of Kārttika or Āśvayuja.
Viṣṇu 86.03: In that regard, one should first of all examine the bull.
Viṣṇu 86.04: [The son] of a cow that has a living calf and is full of milk.
Viṣṇu 86.05: Endowed with all auspicious marks.
Viṣṇu 86.06: Blue.
Or one that is reddish-brown, with the face, tail, feet, and horns being white.
Viṣṇu is the one who covers the herd.

Then, in the midst of the cows, having strewn grass around a well-kindled fire and having cooked a *caru* offering for Pūṣan with milk, and having offered it while reciting, "May Pūṣan follow after our cows; may there be delight here," the smith shall brand the bull.
On one side with a discus, and on the other side with a trident.
One should bathe [the image of] Viṣṇu, marked with [his symbols], with the four verses beginning with "hiraṇyavarṇā" and with the verse "śaṃ no devīḥ."

Having brought [the image of] Viṣṇu, who has been bathed and adorned, together with four heifers that have likewise been bathed and adorned, one should mutter the Rudras, the Puruṣasūkta, and the Kūṣmāṇḍī verses.
"O bull, you are the father of calves"—this one should recite into the right ear of the bull.
And this [verse] from Viṣṇu 86.14:
For the Blessed Lord Dharma is proclaimed to have four feet like a bull;
I choose him with devotion, and may he protect me in every way.

"I give this young man to you as a husband; sport and move about with him, your beloved. May we not be abandoned by our offspring nor by our bodies; may we not fall into the power of the enemy, O King Soma."
One should have a bull yoked with a heifer placed in the northeastern direction;
one should give the officiating priest a pair of garments, as well as gold and bell-metal.
To the iron-smith, a wage should be given according to his heart's desire;
he should provide food with abundant ghee and feed Brāhmaṇas there as well.
In whatever reservoir of water a bull that has been released drinks,
that entire reservoir of water stands as an offering for his ancestors.
Wherever a proud bull scratches the earth with its horn,
that provides abundant food and drink for the ancestors.

Viṣṇu 87.01 Now, on the full moon day of Vaiśākha, having prepared a black antelope skin with its hooves and horns— its horns adorned with gold and its hooves with silver, and decorated with pearls on its tail— one should spread it out upon a woolen cloth.
Then, one should cover it with sesame seeds.
And one should fashion Viṣṇu with a golden navel.
One should cover [the image] with a pair of unwashed garments.
One should have it adorned with all kinds of perfumes and jewels. (Viṣṇu 87.05)

Having visualized four radiant vessels filled with milk, curd, honey, and ghee in the four directions, he should give them to a Brāhmaṇa who maintains the sacred fires, who has been adorned and covered with a pair of garments.
And on this point, there are these verses: Viṣṇu 87.07.
But he who gives a black antelope skin, complete with hooves and horns, covered with sesame seeds and garments, and adorned with all kinds of jewels; [attains the highest world].
By him, the earth—along with its oceans and caves, its mountains, forests, and groves, extending to the four quarters—is considered as given; of this there is no doubt.
He who places sesame seeds, gold, honey, and clarified butter upon a black antelope skin and gives them to a Brahmin overcomes all evil deeds.
Now, when a cow is giving birth, she becomes the earth.
Having given her, thus adorned, to a Brahmin, one obtains the fruit of the gift of the earth.
Regarding this, there is a verse: Viṣṇu 88.03.
Having given a cow with its calf that has two openings [mouths], equal in number to the hairs on its body,
one who is faithful and composed attains heaven for as many ages (*yuga*).
The month of Kārttika has Agni as its presiding deity.
And Agni is the mouth of all the gods.

Therefore, by bathing outdoors during the month of Kārttika, being devoted to the recitation of the Gāyatrī, and eating sacrificial food (haviṣya) even once, one becomes purified from the sins committed throughout the year.

Viṣṇu 89.04: He who bathes daily throughout the entire month of Kārttika, having conquered his senses, reciting prayers, eating sacrificial food (haviṣya), and remaining self-controlled, is liberated from all sins.

Viṣṇu 90.01: On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, when it is joined with the nakṣatra Mṛgaśiras, one should cause a brāhmaṇa to receive at moonrise one *prastha* of powdered salt with a golden center.
By this rite, one is born endowed with beauty and good fortune.

If the full moon day of Pauṣa should coincide with the Puṣya asterism, on that day one whose body has been rubbed with a paste of white mustard seeds, who has been consecrated by being sprinkled from a jar filled with cow’s ghee, and who has bathed with all medicinal herbs, all perfumes, and all seeds— having bathed the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva with ghee, having worshipped him with perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and so forth, and having offered oblations into the fire with Vaiṣṇava, Śākra, and Bārhaspatya mantras— should cause the Brāhmaṇas to pronounce blessings with ghee mixed with gold.
One should give a pair of garments to the performer.
By this action, Viṣṇu is nourished.
If the full moon of Māgha is conjoined with the Maghā nakṣatra, by performing a śrāddha with sesame seeds on that day, one becomes purified.

If the ninth lunar day of Phālguna is joined with the Phalgunī constellation, by offering a well-prepared and well-spread bed to a Brāhmaṇa on that day, one obtains a wife who is pleasing to the mind, beautiful, and wealthy.
Even a woman [should not abandon] her husband. Viṣṇu 90.08.
If the full moon day of Caitra is joined with the Citrā constellation, one attains good fortune by giving beautiful garments on that day.

If the Vaiśākhī full moon is conjoined with the Viśākhā nakṣatra, by satiating seven Brahmins on that day with sesame seeds mixed with honey and thereby pleasing the King of Dharma (Yama), one becomes purified from sins.
Viṣṇu 90.11: If the full moon day of Jyaiṣṭha should coincide with the Jyeṣṭhā nakṣatra, by the gift of an umbrella and sandals on that day, one attains lordship over cattle.
On the full moon day of Āṣāḍha, when it is conjoined with the Āṣāḍhā nakṣatra, by giving food and drink, one obtains that very same [merit] as inexhaustible.
On the full moon day of Śrāvaṇa joined with the Śravaṇa asterism, by giving a water-cow along with food, covered with a pair of garments, one attains heaven.
On the full moon day of Prauṣṭhapada, when it is joined with the Proṣṭhapadā constellation, one becomes completely liberated from all sins by the gift of a cow.
In the month of Āśvayuja, when the moon has entered the asterism Aśvinī, by giving a vessel filled with ghee together with gold to a Brahmin, one becomes possessed of a radiant fire.

If the full moon day of Kārttika should coincide with the Kṛttikā constellation, one who gives on that day a white bull or one of another color—endowed with all kinds of grain, jewels, and perfumes—at the rising of the moon in the midst of lamps to a Brāhmaṇa, shall not behold the fear of the wilderness.

On the third day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, one who has fasted, having worshipped Śrī Vāsudeva with unbroken grains (akṣata), and having offered oblations of those same grains and given them as gifts, becomes purified from all sins.
And whatever one gives on that day, that attains imperishability.

When the twelfth day of the dark fortnight following the full moon of Pauṣa has arrived, one who has fasted, bathed with sesame seeds, offered a libation of sesame, worshipped Vāsudeva with sesame, offered oblations of those same sesame seeds, and given and eaten [sesame], becomes purified from sins.

When the full moon of Māgha has passed, on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight, one who has observed a fast should, upon reaching the asterism Śravaṇa, offer two lamps with two large wicks before Śrī Vāsudeva.
Viṣṇu 90.21: On the right side, having given a complete garment dyed with safflower along with a balance of ghee increased by eight [units].
On the left side, having offered eight [offerings] together with sesame oil, along with a completely white garment.
Having performed this, in whatever kingdom, in whatever region, or in whatever family one is born, one becomes radiant therein.
By giving ghee daily to Brahmins throughout the entire month of Āśvina and thereby pleasing the two Aśvins, one becomes possessed of beauty.
In that very month, by feeding Brāhmaṇas daily with products of the cow, one becomes a sharer of the kingdom.

Viṣṇu 90.26: Every month, when the moon is conjoined with the asterism Revatī, one who feeds Brahmins with milk-rice mixed with honey and clarified butter as the supreme food for the propitiation of Revatī, and thereby pleases Revatī, becomes a possessor of beauty.
In the month of Māgha, having offered oblations of sesame seeds into the fire every day and having fed Brahmins with boiled grain mixed with ghee, one becomes possessed of a radiant digestive fire.
Having bathed in river water on every fourteenth lunar day and having worshipped the King of Dharma (Yama), one becomes purified from all sins. (Viṣṇu 90.28)
If one desires vast enjoyments that reach even the sun and moon during eclipses, one should always bathe in the morning for two months: Māgha and Phālguna.
Viṣṇu 91.01 Now, when water has begun to flow from a well dug by someone, half of that person's evil deeds is destroyed.
The builder of a tank, being eternally satisfied, attains the world of Varuṇa.
One who gives water always remains satisfied.
For one who plants trees, those trees become sons in the next world.
The giver of trees, O Viṣṇu, gratifies the gods with the flowers of those trees.
And [he should honor] guests with fruits. Viṣṇu 91.06.
And with his shadow, he protects those who have approached him.
When the god rains down water, [he satisfies] the ancestors.
One who builds a bridge attains heaven. Viṣṇu 91.09.
Viṣṇu 91.10: One who constructs a temple for a deity attains the very world of that deity for whom he constructs the temple.
Having sprinkled it with nectar, he shines with glory. (Viṣṇu 91.11)
Having performed the *vicitra* [rite], one attains the world of the Gandharvas.
By the offering of flowers, one becomes possessed of splendor.
By the gift of ointment, one becomes possessed of fame. (Viṣṇu 91.14)
By the offering of a lamp, one becomes possessed of keen vision and radiant everywhere.
By the gift of food, one becomes strong. (Viṣṇu 91.16)
By removing the remains of offerings made to a deity, one obtains the fruit of gifting a cow.

[One attains merit] from sweeping the temple of a deity, from smearing it [with cow dung], from cleaning the remnants of a Brahmin's meal, from washing the feet [of the venerable], and from attending to those who are ill.
In the case of wells, groves, tanks, and temples of the gods,
the one who performs the restoration obtains the original merit.
Viṣṇu 92.01: The granting of fearlessness is superior to all other gifts.
By the gift of that, one attains the desired world.
And by the gift of land, O Viṣṇu.
By giving even a piece of land the size of a cow-hide, one becomes purified from all sins.
By the gift of a cow, one attains the heavenly world.
One who gives ten cows [attains] the worlds of the cows.
One who gives a hundred cows [attains] the worlds of Brahmā.

Having given a cow with golden horns, silver hooves, a pearl-adorned tail, a bronze milking vessel, and a cloth as an upper garment, one attains the heavenly world for as many years as there are hairs on that cow.
Especially [the gift of] a tawny cow, O Viṣṇu.
By giving a tamed bull capable of bearing the yoke, one becomes the donor of ten cows.
The giver of a horse attains the same world as the Sun.
One who gives clothing attains the same world as Candra (the Moon).
By the gift of gold, one attains residence in the same world as Agni.
Through the gift of silver, one obtains beauty.
By the gift of vessels made of refined metal, one becomes a recipient of all desires.
Through the gift of ghee, honey, and oil, one attains health. (Viṣṇu 92.16)

Those in the world who follow the vow of the crane and those who bear the marks of a cat fall into the Andhatāmisra hell because of that sinful deed.

With his feet placed upward on his thighs, having laid his other hand upon his left hand, with his tongue motionless against the palate, not touching his teeth with his teeth, gazing at the tip of his own nose and not looking toward the quarters, fearless and with a tranquil self, he should contemplate that which transcends the twenty-four principles.

Now, if one is unable to fix the mark upon the formless [Brahman], then, having first meditated upon each preceding element among earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, self, the unmanifest, and the Puruṣa, and having attained the mark therein, one should abandon that and meditate upon each subsequent one.

Among women who are always well-adorned, devoted to their husbands, speaking kindly, not wasteful with their hands, blessed with sons, careful with household goods, and fond of making offerings— *Viṣṇu* 99.21.

I am ever established in those women whose dwellings are well-cleaned, who have conquered their senses, who are free from strife, who are not covetous, who regard righteousness, who are endowed with compassion, and who are devoted to the Slayer of Madhu.
